title: Make It Easy for Others to Comply
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership opens with a small story: a leader let three hundred cards sit unsigned until a team member left stacks of 25 on the table, and the task was done within a week. The post argues the real lesson is not chunking but lowering the friction of compliance. Its move is to reframe apparent procrastination or resistance as inconvenience, not unwillingness. It offers a list of practical tactics, such as templates, step-by-step instructions, pre-addressed envelopes, scripted openings and keeping tools within reach. The takeaway for leaders is to take responsibility for making requests easy to fulfil instead of blaming the person who has not done them.
points: A stalled task is often a design problem: the request is onerous or inconvenient, not resisted.
Breaking a large job into small stacks is one way, but only one way, to make compliance easier.
Concrete aids such as templates, scripted first lines, and tools set within reach remove the friction that causes delay.
Leaders who simplify requests spare everyone unnecessary frustration.
quotes: Then, a team member did something creative. They placed a stack of just 25 cards on the table and asked the leader to sign them before leaving for the day.
The industrious team member didn’t just break an unwieldy task into bite-sized chunks. They did something even more important. They made it easier for the leader to comply.
Whenever anyone procrastinates on a task or seems to resist complying with instructions or requests, it may be that they find the requirement onerous or it may be that it is simply hard to comply.
When leaders need anyone to do or complete a task they don’t seem to get around to, the best idea is to make it easier for them to comply.
People appear to resist when it is difficult to comply. It’s usually not true. They aren’t resisting as much as they find the task inconvenient or hard.
Good leaders go out of their way to make complying with any request much easier. This saves everyone from unnecessary frustration.
